title: Markdown to HTML converter
prompt:
Build a Markdown to HTML converter in Python as a package md/ with md/__init__.py, md/inline.py, md/blocks.py and md/__main__.py. - md/inline.py: render_inline(text) -> str. First escape & < > as & < >. Then: `code` -> code (nothing inside a code span is changed further), [text](url) -> text, **bold** -> bold, *italic* -> italic (bold is handled before italic). - md/blocks.py: convert(markdown) -> str. Blocks are separated by blank lines. A line starting with 1 to 6 # and a space is a heading

..

to
..
(a heading is always its own block, even without blank lines around it). Consecutive lines starting with "- " make one
    with an
  • per line. Any other run of lines is a paragraph

    ..

    with its lines joined by one space and trimmed. All text inside blocks goes through render_inline. The blocks are joined with " " (no other newlines, no trailing newline); empty input gives "". Example: convert("# Hi Some *text* here - a - b") == "

    Hi

    Some text here

    • a
    • b
    " - md/__main__.py: `python -m md input.md output.html` writes the converted file. md/__init__.py exposes convert. Write unit tests too.
